--[[
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
--                               SkillUtils                                       --
--                                                                                --
-- This module includes functions for dealing with skill success chances          --
-- and other calculations. It is a meta-module, and is not designed to be         --
-- called directly from #invoke.                                                  --
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
--]]

local libraryUtil = require('libraryUtil')
local arr = require('Module:Array')
local nb = require('Module:Probability').nbinomial
local trees = require('Module:SkillUtils/TreeData')
local hatchets = require('Module:SkillUtils/HatchetData').hatchets
local seeds = require('Module:SkillUtils/SeedData')

local p = {}

local floor = math.floor
local infinity = math.huge
local checkType = libraryUtil.checkType
local checkTypeMulti = libraryUtil.checkTypeMulti

-- Used for matching seed/hatchet/tree names 
-- Ignores case and space/underscore
local function match_ignore_case(base, search)
	local function generic_str(pattern)
	  local subbed = pattern:gsub("(%a)", 
	  	function(letter)
	      return string.format("[%s%s]", letter:lower(), letter:upper())
		end):gsub(" ", "[ _]")
	  return subbed
	end
	return base:match(generic_str(search))
end

local function get_record(array, search_field, thing)
	local item, _ = arr.find(array, 
		function (search) 
			return match_ignore_case(search[search_field], thing)
		end
	)
	return item
end

-- Block of functions to get matching records from integer-indexed tables
function p.get_tree_record(tree)
	return get_record(trees, "name", tree)
end

function p.get_hatchet_record(hatchet)
	return get_record(hatchets, "short", hatchet) or get_record(hatchets, "label", hatchet)
end

function p.get_seed_record(seed)
	return get_record(seeds, "seed", seed)
end

--
-- it's worth noting that this isn't a monotonically increasing function. There are dips
-- when the two different integer divisions change magnitude at different rates, resulting
-- in some rather unintuitive behavior where increasing skill level can actually decrease
-- success chance.
--
function p.jagex_interpolate(low, high, level)
	return math.floor((low*(99-level))/98) + math.floor((high*(level-1))/98)
end

-- "mult" added here to accomodate woodcutting, which does some unique stuff 
function p.stat_roll(low, high, level, mult)
	mult = mult or 1
	return (p.jagex_interpolate(low, high, level) + 1)/(256 * mult)
end

-- Extra chance and extra chance trials are added in with the farmer's outfit in mind
-- They add an extra chance to save harvest lives when farming crops
-- If extra_chance_trials is 0, which it defaults to, this is equivalent to the 
-- expected total number of trials (see above for more detail).
-- Technically what we've modeled is a discrete phase-type distribution, but 
-- it's also just two different negative binomials glued together.
function p.farming_yield(low, high, level, mult, lives, extra_chance_trials, extra_chance)
	extra_chance_trials = extra_chance_trials or 0
	local base_chance = 1 - p.stat_roll(low, high, level, mult)
	extra_chance = 1 - extra_chance
	local first_set = nb.trials(base_chance, extra_chance_trials)*(1/extra_chance)
	local last_set = nb.trials(base_chance, lives - extra_chance_trials)
	return first_set + last_set
end

-- Simple step size function
function p.simple_scale(value, from, to)
    return math.floor((value * to) / from)
end

-- There's some specific-skill related stuff we'll add here too
function p.woodcutting_low_high(chop_chance, tool_power, chop_ratio)
    chop_chance = chop_chance * 10000
    chop_ratio = chop_ratio or 31250
    local tier_increment = math.floor(chop_chance / 2)
    local low = chop_chance + p.simple_scale(tier_increment, 100, tool_power - 100)
    local high = p.simple_scale(low, 10000, chop_ratio)
    return low, high
end

-- Tie it together in a nice function for usage outside
function p.woodcutting_chance(chop_chance, tool_power, chop_ratio, level, mult)
	local low, high = p.woodcutting_low_high(chop_chance, tool_power, chop_ratio)
	return p.stat_roll(low, high, level, mult)
end

-- This is different from the Module:Array 'clone()'; this works on pairs, not ipairs
function p.shallow_copy(from, to)
    local orig_type = type(from)
    if orig_type == 'table' then
        local copy = to or {}
        for orig_key, orig_value in pairs(from) do
            copy[orig_key] = orig_value
        end
        return copy
    else -- number, string, boolean, etc
        return from
    end
end

return p
